title: The Night Journey and the Hijra
hook: after the night journey and the pledges at 'Aqabah, he slips out of Mecca, hides in a cave, and tells Abu Bakr: do not grieve, Allah is with us

segments.voice: Yesterday, the road from Ta'if: stoned, bleeding, and offered revenge, he hoped for their children instead. Your line was not them their children. Day ninety-five.

After Ta'if, a night. The Qur'an opens its seventeenth surah with it, in Pickthall's words: “Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far Distant Place of Worship.” From Mecca to Jerusalem in one night, the Isra, and then, Muslims say, up through the heavens, the Mi'raj, where the five daily prayers were given. Most scholars say it was a journey of body and soul; some early voices said it was of the spirit. Either way, after the year of sorrow, it came as an honor and a comfort. And then, at the pilgrimage season, a door opens. Men from a town called Yathrib meet him at night at a place called 'Aqabah, and pledge to protect him as they would their own families.
screen: `THE NIGHT JOURNEY.` → `THE FIVE PRAYERS GIVEN.` → `A PLEDGE AT 'AQABAH.`

segments.voice: So the Muslims of Mecca begin to leave for Yathrib, quietly, a few at a time, leaving houses and businesses behind. Quraysh realize what's happening, and the leaders decide: before he can go, kill him. One young man from each clan, so the blame is shared and his family can't take revenge on anyone. The Qur'an mentions their plotting. That night, the Prophet ﷺ asks 'Ali to sleep in his bed, under his green cloak. And he slips out with Abu Bakr. Instead of heading north toward Yathrib, where everyone would look, they go south, and climb to a cave on Mount Thawr. They hide there three nights. Abu Bakr's daughter Asma' brings them food, tearing her waistband in two to tie up the bundles. And the trackers come, right up to the mouth of the cave. Abu Bakr whispers: if one of them looks down at his feet, he'll see us. And the Prophet ﷺ answers, in a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari: what do you think of two, when Allah is the third? The Qur'an remembers that moment, in Surah At-Tawbah. The Prophet was “the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us.” People also tell a story of a spider that spun a web across the cave's mouth, and a dove that nested there, so the trackers thought no one could be inside; the Qur'an doesn't mention it, and scholars differ on how reliable the report is. The trackers leave. And the two set out for Yathrib. This leaving is called the hijra: the migration, the breaking away. It is the hinge of Islamic history.
screen: `ONE MAN FROM EACH CLAN.` · `'ALI SLEEPS IN HIS BED.` · `THREE NIGHTS IN THE CAVE OF THAWR.` · `WHAT OF TWO, WHEN ALLAH IS THIRD?` · then, large: `GRIEVE NOT. LO! ALLAH IS WITH US.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Find a small, enclosed place, if you can: a closet, a car, the corner of a room, or just cup your hands over your eyes. Make it your cave. Breathe. Let one fear come in with you, something that feels like it's right at the entrance. Then whisper, so quietly only you can hear it. If you pray: Allah is with us. If you don't: I'm not alone in here. Say it a few times, slowly. Then sit, and listen to your own breathing. The bell holds the time.
Hijra. The migration: the Prophet's leaving of Mecca for Yathrib, breaking with the old to begin again.
Your line: Allah is with us. Today, when something scary is at the entrance, whisper your line once before you walk out. Tomorrow, the last day of the stories. Day ninety-five.

howItsDone: Muslims mark the Isra and Mi'raj on the 27th of Rajab in many communities, and the Islamic year begins from the Hijra; 9:40 is often recited for courage in hard moments.

fork.setup: two men hide in a cave. the trackers are at the entrance. one whispers: if they look down, they'll see us. what does the other say?
options: grieve not; Allah is with us.
fork.reveal: grieve not. lo! Allah is with us (9:40). and in Bukhari: what do you think of two, when Allah is the third?

trapdoor: what you thought: the Prophet moved to Medina.
what it means: hunted by a plot to kill him, he slipped out at night, hid three days in a cave, and left his home city for a new beginning.

what a scholar hears: 9:40 calls him thani ithnayn, the second of two; the word hijra also means leaving behind what is wrong, and a hadith calls the true emigrant the one who leaves what Allah forbids.

notes: Pickthall 17:1 and 9:40 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording.

Isra and Mi'raj: 'most scholars say body and soul; some early voices said spirit' (reports from 'Aishah and Mu'awiyah). Confirm framing. The 27th of Rajab date is customary in many communities, not universal.
Two pledges of 'Aqabah compressed into one sentence; confirm.
The spider and dove: reported in Musnad Ahmad and later seerah with a disputed chain; the script calls it a story people tell. Hadith number from memory; confirm.
Voice includes the Prophet's words via hadith paraphrase; the fork is told in third person deliberately.
